registration.title: Skill scores adjusted for the league they are played in
registration.what: Each skill score takes off an offset for each league the player's minutes were in, fitted from players who played 900+ minutes a season in more than one league, so League Two output counts for less than Premier League output. Only the skill scores change; the ranks don't read them.
registration.why: The owner, 2026-10-22: D. Markanday (Chesterfield, League Two) scores 90 finishing, 88 creating and 96 dribbling but is 70 overall. The scores set every league's output per 90 against each other with no allowance for the level.
registration.how: skill_units, skill_league_offsets and the rating window's league minutes in player_ratings.py (experiments/skill_league/DESIGN.md).
registration.hypothesis: A player's skill z in one league, moved by the two leagues' offsets, predicts his z in another league the next season better than his z as it was.
registration.success_criteria: experiments/skill_league/run.py: at least 200 later moves between leagues, a lower squared error averaged over the seven skills with its 95% interval below 0, lower in at least 5 of 7 skills, and every rank and predicted XI identical.

events.label: Skill z in a new league the next season, predicted from the old league's: mean squared error over the seven skills, 606 moves into 2025 or later, offsets fitted on seasons to 2024
events.meaningful: About 7.7% lower error, lower in 6 of 7 skills (dribbling slightly higher). The registered check 'ranks untouched' came out false only because it compares the to_rank function passed to the writer, two objects that are never equal; every rank, season rank, position rank, projection and predicted XI was identical. Under the evaluator as written the verdict is FAILED.

events.text: experiments/skill_league/run.py compares every argument of _write but the skill scores, including to_rank, a function: base and changed can never be equal there, whatever the change. The design's check (DESIGN.md, check 4: ranks and predicted XIs identical) holds on every data output (results.json, identical_outputs). The evaluator is left as it is; the owner decides.

events.reason: Owner, 2026-10-22: release it. The only failed check was the evaluator comparing a function (event 2); every rank and predicted XI was identical, and the scores predict a player's numbers in another league about 7.7% better.

events.note: Released at its registered settings (900-minute units, offsets shrunk by n / (n + 30)), fitted each run on every unit, as MC-0032 on 2026-10-22.
